references.text: Describes the story of the manna given from heaven in the wilderness, which Jesus directly refers to when he says it was not Moses who gave the bread, but the Father.
Proclaims that God gave 'grain from heaven' and that people ate 'bread of angels', an expression that underlies Jesus' claim about the true bread from heaven.
Mentions that God gave 'bread from heaven' and opened the heavens to provide them with grain, emphasizing God's role as the giver, in contrast to Moses who was only the mediator.
Reminds us that God fed the people with manna to show that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes out of God's mouth, a theme Jesus expands on in the same chapter.
Jesus' own explanation in the same chapter where he identifies himself as 'the true bread' that came down from heaven, in direct contrast to the manna of the fathers.
